title: Publish flow for sparse-model variants with cost-sampling
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: We need a deterministic publish workflow for performance profiles that includes sparse model variants (e.g., head-pruned, quantized-4bit, trimmed KV-cache builds) and realistic per-token cost estimates derived from sampled production-like traffic. Current publication flow assumes monolithic model artifacts and synthetic benchmarks; it doesn't capture variant behavior or representative cost under real mixing of sequence lengths and batch distributions.

Goal: Define and implement an end-to-end publish flow that: 1) records variant-to-base mappings and hardware anchors, 2) runs lightweight sampled shadowing (cost-sampling) to measure token-level cost and latency distributions for each variant on target hardware, 3) generates a signed performance manifest (latency/throughput/cost) that can be pinned by customers, and 4) exposes automated rollback criteria and a provenance ledger for audits.

Scope: This ticket covers the product definition (fields, safety checks, UI surfaces), the sampling policy (percent of traffic, traffic shaping), verification gating rules (latency P95/P99 thresholds, cost divergence limits), and consumer-facing messaging (Console + API changes). Implementation and infra tasks will be split to ENG tickets after product signoff.
acceptance_criteria: Performance manifest schema includes: base_model_tag, variant_tag, hardware_anchor, kernel_profile_hash, sample_window_ms, cost_per_1e3_tokens_estimate
Sampling job definition documented and runnable in staging with <1% synthetic traffic shadowing and configurable seed
Automated attestation produces pass/fail with reasons (latency_slip, cost_delta, correctness_regression) and attaches signed artifact to catalog entry
Console: variant mapping visible under model page with clear pin button and rollback affordance
API: publish endpoint returns signed_manifest_url and verification_summary
Rollback triggers documented and mapped to automated canary or manual actions
tasks: Propose sampling policy and default percent (PM+ENG)
Design console UI for variant pinning and manifest drilldown (DES ticket)
Create ENG spike for shadow-sampling harness and cost aggregation
Define attestation rules and threshold matrix
Coordinate with Security to sign manifests and key rotation process
Write release notes and customer-facing FAQ
comments: 2026-01-22 Alyssa Chen: Initial draft completed; included example fields and sketch of sampling approach. Uploaded draft spec to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/Sparse+Variant+Publish+Flow
2026-01-28 Diego Morales: Discussed with infra - ENG wants an opt-in flag for shadow sampling per-customer to reduce noise in production. Added as decision point.

2026-02-03 Design review (Dana Iqbal): Suggested adding a visual timeline to Console showing when sampling occurred and which requests were shadowed; flagged that we need to mask PII in sampled payloads.

2026-02-10 Engineering spike complete: ENG-59821 created for harness. Preliminary numbers show pruning-only variants increase latency variance at high sequence lengths; saved artifact at: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-tools/pull/427
2026-02-16 SRE note (Kofi Mensah): Sampling at 1% on peak services increases p95 by ~0.2ms—within SLO but recommend staging shadow first. Added dependency on ENG-61002 for rate-limit guardrails.
2026-02-24 PM update: Consolidated attestation matrix; uploaded signed_manifest schema example and test vectors to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-perf-manifests

2026-02-28 Diego Morales: Locking scope for MVP: support three variant classes (quantized, head-pruned, trimmed-kv); sampling default 0.5% for hosted, 0% for Dedicated until opt-in. Moving to In Progress. ENG owners assigned to ENG-59821 and ENG-61002.
notes: Trade-offs: higher sampling shows more accurate cost but risks load on latency-sensitive paths; opted for low-percent shadowing plus synthetic replay in staging
Edge cases: variants that change tokenizer behavior must be rejected by attestation (correctness_regression). Will add check to diff generative outputs on canonical prompts.
Auditability: manifests will include git commit + container digest + signing-key-id to support later provenance checks
